profile.a: The five-person Global Consulting Project team, writing the final report.
BlackRock's Real Estate Research Team; BlackRock managed nearly $12 trillion at December 2024.
How BlackRock can responsibly and effectively adopt AI to improve its real estate investment capability and decisions.
Handed in on 22 April 2025, after weekly client meetings and interviews from 20 March to 14 April 2025.
BlackRock's global portfolio of direct commercial real estate investments.
AI is reshaping real estate value drivers, and opaque models clash with BlackRock's duty to explain decisions to investors, clients and the public.

Over 30 outreach attempts led to more than 10 informal conversations and 5 formal interviews (2 academic, 2 industry, 1 AI), backed by secondary research, a risk matrix and the three-horizon framework.

charts.title: From outreach to evidence: how the primary research narrowed
charts.takeaway: One in six approaches became a formal interview. The report's sector and adoption conclusions rest on these five conversations plus secondary sources, a limit the team itself acknowledges.

charts.title: Formal interviews by expertise
charts.takeaway: A deliberately balanced panel, but with one AI specialist the technical claims about explainability rest on a single expert view.

charts.title: Winners and losers by asset class
text: Front runner: AI supply chains, e-commerce
charts.takeaway: The implication for BlackRock: adjust exposure towards tech-aligned, service-oriented assets, and reposition office and retail before they become obsolete.

charts.title: The three research questions and what the report answers
rows: How does AI change real estate demand and behaviour?
A fourth wave after mechanisation, urbanisation and globalisation; buildings become services and asset management matters as much as acquisition.
How can AI be used in investment strategy?
Across the lifecycle: lease abstraction, GPT-powered underwriting tools, sentiment analysis, automated valuation and risk forecasting, all dependent on integrated data.
What are the risks and how are they mitigated?
Explainability, data bias and fair-housing compliance; SHAP and LIME, prompt rules, stop lists, classifiers and human oversight; the structured AI judgement process.

charts.title: Roadmap recommended to BlackRock

items.label: Consolidate data into a unified platform
Pilot proven AI in deals and due diligence
Scale cloud, governance and partnerships (e.g. OpenAI)
Embed AI in strategy; digital twins; AI-era infrastructure

charts.takeaway: In the final report, partnering with providers replaces the deck's in-house language model, following the expert warning that custom models date quickly.
